blocks.text: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks are a type of injection in which malicious scripts are injected into otherwise benign and trusted websites. XSS attacks occur when an attacker uses a web application to send malicious code, generally in the form of a browser side script, to a different end user.

items: **Reflected XSS**: Script is reflected off the web server
**Stored XSS**: Script is permanently stored on the target server
**DOM-based XSS**: Vulnerability exists in client-side code

blocks.text: Submit JavaScript code in various input points and observe if the code gets executed in the browser.
See `xss-payloads.txt` for a comprehensive list of XSS payloads.

See `context-sanitizer-payloads.txt` for HTML, attribute, JavaScript and URL contexts; sanitizer, DOM clobbering, CSP and Trusted Types inputs. Select the section matching the target input context. Match the browser insertion context and sanitizer configuration, and verify script execution in an isolated browser fixture.

See `advanced-xss-payloads.txt` for Blind XSS loaders, JSONP callback abuse, Markdown-renderer XSS, CSP bypass patterns, mutation XSS, sanitiser probes and modern execution contexts. See also `DOM-Based-Attacks/` for source-to-sink and `postMessage` cases.

sections.label: Advanced XSS Payloads: Blind, JSONP, Markdown, CSP Bypass, mXSS and Modern Contexts
Blind XSS (stored, rendered later in an internal or admin view): callback loader variants
Blind XSS in headers and out-of-band fields that internal tools may render
JSONP callback abuse (the callback name is reflected unescaped as JavaScript)
JSONP used to satisfy a CSP script-src allowing a host (load as script from an allowed domain)
Markdown renderer XSS (link, image, autolink, raw HTML passthrough)
CSP bypass: unsafe-inline missing; script gadgets in allow-listed libraries (CSP script-src 'self' or CDN host)
CSP bypass: strict-dynamic and nonce reuse / injection
CSP bypass: dangling markup to steal the nonce or token (no script execution needed)
CSP bypass: missing directives (form-action, base-uri, object-src, frame-ancestors, default-src fallback)
CSP bypass: allowed-host user content (script-src allows a host that serves user uploads)
CSP bypass: Service Worker and script-src 'self' with an upload that serves JavaScript
Mutation XSS (mXSS): input that is safe when sanitised but mutates when reparsed through innerHTML
Sanitiser configuration probes (what the allow-list permits)
DOM clobbering against sanitisers (see also DOM-Based-Attacks)
Dynamic import and modern JavaScript execution contexts
Event handlers that fire without user interaction (HTML contexts that strip common handlers)

sections.label: Context-Specific XSS and Sanitizer Regression Fixtures
HTML fragment context: execution markers, no credential access or external callbacks
Single-quoted attribute context: manual focus/pointer interaction may be required
Unquoted attribute context: whitespace can introduce another attribute only if the sink is truly unquoted
Script-element boundary: HTML parsing can terminate a script regardless of the surrounding JS string
DOM clobbering fixtures: only matter when application code reads named DOM properties as configuration
Trusted Types fixture: run in an isolated page with require-trusted-types-for 'script'
CSP fixtures: nonce handling is a server policy test; never insert a real production nonce into this file
